<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXIII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|207 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 1. 11. Mr. 15, 1. Io. 18, 27.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ GOOD FRIDAY.}}∷ all the multitude of them rising vp, led him to Pilate. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=2}}† And they began to accuse him, saying, VVe haue found this man subuerting our nation, & prohibiting to giue tributes to Cæsar, and saying that he is Christ the king. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=3}}† And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the king of the Ievves? But he ansvvering said, Thou sayest. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=4}}† And Pilate said to the cheefe Priests and multitudes, I finde no cause in this man. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=5}}† But they vvere more earnest, saying, He stirreth the people teaching through out al Ievvrie, beginning from Galilee euen hither. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=6}}† But Pilate hearing Galilee, asked if the man vvere of Galilee. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=7}}† And vvhen he vnderstoode that he vvas of Herods iurisdiction, he sent him backe to Herod, vvho vvas also him self at Hierusalem in those daies.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=8}}† And Herod seeing {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvas very glad, for he vvas desirous of a long time to see him, for because he heard many things of him: and he hoped to see some signe vvrought by him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=9}}† And he asked him in many vvordes. But he ansvvered him nothing. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=10}}† And there stoode the cheefe Priests and the Scribes constantly accusing him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=11}}† And Herod vvith his armie set him at naught: and he mocked him, putting on him a vvhite garment, and sent him backe to Pilate. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=12}}† And Herod and Pilate vvere made frendes that day. for before they vvere enemies one to an other.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=13}}† And Pilate calling together the cheefe Priests and magistrates, and the people, {{verse|chapter=23|verse=14}}† said to them, You haue presented vnto me this man, as auerting the people, and behold I examining him before you, haue found no cause in this man of those things vvherein you accuse him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=15}}† No, nor Herod neither. for I sent you to him, and behold, nothing vvorthie of death is done to him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=16}}† I vvil chasten him therfore and dimisse him.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
